To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
radiation-induced rat skin tumors contain c-myc and/or K-ras oncogenic alterations.
radiation-induced rat tumors have activation of c-myc or c-K-ras or both.
ionizing radiation can activate oncogenes and that the activation of these oncogenes may be associated with tumor formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of oncogenes in rat primary tumors and the role of the oncogenes in tumorigenesis.
the molecular biology of carcinogenesis, with emphasis on the role of the c-myc protooncogene in radiation-induced tumorigenesis.
the molecular mechanisms of tumor induction by ionizing radiation, with the ultimate goal of identifying the critical molecular changes that occur in the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the K-ras onc gene is activated in 50% of the radiation-induced tumors, and c-myc gene is amplified in 90% of the tumors.
the K-ras oncogenic sequence is activated by point mutations, and that the c-myc gene is amplified and rearranged in a subset of rat primary tumors induced by ionising radiation.
the activation of c-myc is not a specific event in radiation carcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiation induces activation of both the c-myc and the K-ras genes in rat skin tumors, and the c-myc gene is amplified in some of the tumors.
radiation-induced rat skin tumors contain activated K-ras and c-myc oncogenes, and the presence of both oncogenes is associated with the histologic appearance of clear cell carcinomas.   1
the activation of c-myc is the most frequent event in radiation-induced rat tumors, followed by K-ras, and that both events are more frequent in clear cell carcinomas than in squamous carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the activation of oncogenes in radiation-induced rat skin tumors is not random but is associated with specific patterns of activation that are consistent with the histopathologic classification of the tumors.
radiation-induced tumors are heterogeneous with regard to the activation of specific oncogenes.
the c-myc oncogene is activated in the majority of primary rat tumors induced with ionizing radiation.
